title: Within-month rain order gave little modeled runoff change in 119 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We tested whether changes in rain order within a month can make the post-1997 runoff loss in south-east Australia. We fitted a continuous daily soil-water and routing model before 1997 at 119 CAMELS-AUS v2.03 catchments. Thirty permutations kept all daily rain amounts and monthly totals. In 2010-2021, the change in modeled flow due to actual order relative to these permutations was +0.54 mm/year with AGCD rain (conditional 95% interval -1.46 to +3.03) and +0.47 with SILO (-1.32 to +2.82). These modeled order changes are small and do not match a 40 mm/year loss. With actual rain order, the model retained a deficit of -50.15 mm/year with AGCD (-72.40 to -29.25) and -21.46 with SILO (-45.59 to +0.34). Earlier validation point biases were also negative. The narrow result limits within-month order effects in this fixed model. It does not exclude daily rainfall mechanisms in other models or identify a physical cause. Rain source, simple stores, no snow, limited optimization, selected records and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Code, source hashes, fitted and annual statistics, all uncertainty draws and numerical checks are included. External daily observations stay outside the package.

display.caption: Daily-model annual residuals and change in the modeled rain-order effect. Intervals condition on the model fits and the 30-permutation ensemble. Rain-order values compare actual order with within-month permutations, then subtract the reference mean. They do not measure a causal effect.
